page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or a GPU, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the ecs.hfr7.3xlarge in the average performance tier across most tested workloads. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is measured at 1577.28, while multi-core performance reaches 12473.75. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 698.81 GB/sec, which drops to 69.85 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write speed of 46.64 GB/sec. In database operations, the instance achieves a PassMark database score of 4736.01 and processes 11.99 million Redis SET operations per second. For language model workloads, the instance processes 767.53 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model, but performance drops to a weak tier of 17.76 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The lack of bundled local storage means storage must be attached network-wise, which is a tradeoff to consider for disk-heavy applications. The hardware profile is best suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, caching layers such as Redis, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing tasks.
